title: Col. William Russell III
summary: Born in Virginia in 1758, William Russell III fought at Kings Mountain, settled Fayette County in 1783, and sat in Kentucky’s early legislature.
bodyMarkdown:
[William Russell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Russell_%28Kentucky_politician%29) was born on March 6, 1758, in Culpeper County, Virginia. His parents were William and Tabitha (Adams) Russell. His father was a prominent figure in southwestern Virginia and later a colonel in the Continental Army.

## The 1773 attempt

In 1773 the elder Russell took his family west with a party guided by Daniel Boone. It was the first attempt to establish a permanent white settlement in Kentucky. The party turned back after a fatal attack by Native warriors. Boone's son James and Henry Russell, a son of William Sr., were captured and killed.

## Revolution and settlement

During the Revolution, Russell served as a captain in the Virginia militia. At the Battle of Kings Mountain he was an aide to Col. William Campbell. At the war's end he moved to Kentucky. In 1783 he settled in Fayette County on land granted to his father for military service.

## Militia and the War of 1812

Russell led Kentucky militia as a colonel in the Northwest Indian War. In the War of 1812 he commanded the 7th Infantry Regiment. In September 1812, passing through Vincennes, he led regulars, rangers and militia to [relieve the besieged Fort Harrison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siege_of_Fort_Harrison) in Indiana Territory. The Native force there departed when his column arrived.

In October 1812 he and Illinois governor Ninian Edwards led an expedition that [destroyed Potawatomi and Kickapoo villages](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peoria_War) in the Peoria area, and the residents abandoned the area. On July 1, 1813, he set out with at least 700 mounted rangers on a month-long raid of about 500 miles through Indiana Territory. The force burned a stockade in what is now Miami County, Indiana, and destroyed five Native villages.

For the Native families of the region, these campaigns meant the loss of their towns; the 1813 raiders returned to Fort Harrison without losing a soldier.

## In the legislature

Russell represented his district in the Virginia legislature in 1790 and 1791. After statehood he served in the Kentucky House in 1792, from 1796 to 1800, in 1802 and again in 1823. He died on July 3, 1825.

## Kentucky today

[Russell County](https://grokipedia.com/page/Russell_County,_Kentucky) was formed on December 14, 1825, from parts of Adair, Cumberland and Wayne counties, and was named for him. Its seat is Jamestown. Fort Russell Township in Illinois also carries his name. The town of [Russellville](/stories/russellville-from-big-boiling-spring-to-county-seat/) and Russell County, Virginia, were named for his father instead.
